decision: Exercise the real mkdir-to-owner-publication crash window with a bounded fault hook, and permit age-based recovery only for a genuinely ownerless lock directory after orphan grace.
problem: The filesystem lock intentionally permits age-based recovery when the lock directory exists but owner.json is absent. That is necessary for a crash between mkdir(lock) and owner publication, but until now the OS-process campaign only tested crashes after owner metadata existed.

reviews.correctness: Preferred fault injection at the exact publication boundary so the test proves the production recovery branch rather than approximating it by manually creating a directory.
reviews.robustness_security: Preferred a bounded ownerless grace: acquisition before grace must time out, while recovery after grace may proceed only when owner.json is genuinely absent. Corrupt or unreadable published metadata remains fail-closed and is not age-reclaimed.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Preferred an optional local callback used only for fault injection/observability. It adds no filesystem operation, network round trip, Qubes dependency, or production latency when unset, and avoids introducing a database or lock daemon into Slice 1.

alternatives_rejected: Create an ownerless lock directory directly in the test: cheaper, but does not prove the real mkdir-to-publication crash window in withFileMutationLock.
Disable ownerless age recovery entirely: fail-closed but can permanently wedge a durable store after a legitimate crash before owner publication.
Reclaim any unreadable owner metadata after a timeout: unsafe because corrupt metadata may still belong to a live writer and would turn metadata damage into an ownership bypass.
qa: Spawn a separate Node process that creates the lock directory and pauses before owner.json publication.
Kill that process to leave the real ownerless crash artifact.
Verify acquisition before orphanGraceMs fails rather than stealing the lock.
Verify acquisition after orphanGraceMs succeeds and reports finite lock-wait telemetry.
Retain corrupt/unreadable owner metadata fail-closed tests and normal dead-owner/process-instance recovery tests.
failure_lessons: A stale-lock policy needs separate rules for unpublished ownership and corrupt published ownership; treating both as 'missing metadata' weakens fencing.
Fault injection is most valuable at the exact durability/ownership boundary. Synthetic filesystem setup can miss ordering bugs in the production control flow.
remaining_risks: orphanGraceMs is a same-host filesystem heuristic and still requires measured recovery/lock-wait latency on target storage.
The filesystem lock is not a distributed lock across multiple coordinator machines.
Slice 1 still requires green executable QA before Qubes transport/qualification is built on top of it.
